# Ezra Chapter 8 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 470r–470v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EZR_008_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Here is a list of the family leaders and their registered descendants who traveled with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes:

**2** From the family of Phinehas: Gershom. From Ithamar: Daniel. From David: Hattush. **3** From Parosh (through Shecaniah): Zechariah, with 150 registered men. **4** From Pahath-moab: Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, with 200 men. **5** From Shecaniah: the son of Jahaziel, with 300 men. **6** From Adin: Ebed son of Jonathan, with 50 men. **7** From Elam: Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, with 70 men. **8** From Shephatiah: Zebadiah son of Michael, with 80 men. **9** From Joab: Obadiah son of Jehiel, with 218 men. **10** From Shelomith: the son of Josiphiah, with 160 men. **11** From Bebai: Zechariah son of Bebai, with 28 men. **12** From Azgad: Johanan son of Hakkatan, with 110 men. **13** From Adonikam (the last to come): Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah, with 60 men. **14** From Bigvai: Uthai and Zaccur, with 70 men.

**15** I assembled everyone at the canal that flows toward Ahava, and we camped there for three days. When I reviewed the group, I found plenty of laypeople and priests but not a single Levite.

**16** So I summoned the leaders Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam, along with Joiarib and Elnathan, who were men of learning. **17** I sent them to Iddo, the leader of the community at Casiphia, and told them exactly what to say: ask Iddo and his associates, the temple servants at Casiphia, to send us people to serve in the temple of our God.

**18** Because God's gracious hand was on us, they sent us Sherebiah — a capable man from the family of Mahli son of Levi — along with his sons and relatives, 18 in all. **19** They also sent Hashabiah, together with Jeshaiah from the family of Merari, and his relatives and their sons — 20 people. **20** They also provided 220 temple servants, from the group that David and his officials had originally assigned to assist the Levites. All of them were registered by name.

**21** There by the Ahava canal, I called for a time of fasting and prayer, so that we could humble ourselves before God and ask him for a safe journey for us, our children, and all our possessions. **22** I was too embarrassed to ask the king for soldiers and cavalry to protect us on the road. After all, I had told the king, "Our God protects everyone who trusts in him, but his fierce anger falls on those who abandon him." **23** So we fasted and prayed earnestly, and God heard our prayer.

**24** I then chose twelve of the leading priests — Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their relatives — **25** and weighed out to them the silver, gold, and articles that the king, his advisors, his nobles, and all the Israelites present had donated for the temple.

**26** I weighed out into their care: 25 tons of silver, silver articles worth 7,500 pounds, 7,500 pounds of gold, **27** twenty gold bowls worth about 19 pounds each, and two articles of polished bronze, as precious as gold.

**28** I told them, "You are set apart for the LORD, and these articles are sacred. The silver and gold are a freewill offering to the LORD, the God of your ancestors. **29** Guard them carefully until you can weigh them out in the presence of the leading priests, the Levites, and the family leaders of Israel at the temple in Jerusalem."

**30** So the priests and Levites took responsibility for the silver, gold, and sacred articles, to transport them to the temple of our God in Jerusalem.

**31** We left the Ahava canal on the twelfth day of the first month and headed for Jerusalem. God's hand protected us, and he kept us safe from enemies and bandits along the way.

**32** We arrived in Jerusalem and rested for three days. **33** On the fourth day, we went to the temple and weighed out all the silver, gold, and articles. They were entrusted to the priest Meremoth son of Uriah and his associate Eleazar son of Phinehas, along with the Levites Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui. **34** Everything was counted and weighed, and the total weight was officially recorded.

**35** Then the returned exiles offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering — all as a burnt offering to the LORD.

**36** They also delivered the king's orders to the royal officials and governors of the province west of the Euphrates, who then gave their support to the people and to the temple of God.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 15 — No Levites:** This is a deeply telling detail. Of the roughly 1,500 men who volunteered to return with Ezra, not one was a Levite. The people who were supposed to serve in the temple had to be specifically recruited. Sometimes those closest to sacred work are the most reluctant to sacrifice for it.

**Verses 21-23 — Faith on the line:** Ezra's dilemma is profoundly human. He had spoken boldly about God's protection — and now he had to live by his own words. Asking for a military escort would have been the sensible thing, but it would have contradicted his testimony. So instead he fasted and prayed. This is one of the Bible's most honest portraits of what it costs to trust God publicly.

**Verse 28 — "You are holy to the LORD":** Ezra declares the priests holy, the vessels holy, and the offerings holy — sanctifying the entire journey. The road from Babylon to Jerusalem was not just a physical journey; it was a sacred procession. Every step was an act of worship.

*— PNEUMA*
